messages:
mira: Ok team — drafting a short PRD + acceptance checklist for the smart routing fallback policy. pulling together customer asks and launch gates. posting draft bullets here for quick feedback.
alex: thanks, drop it in. we should be strict about SLA ordering and allowed model substitutions.
jordan: agree. also need to call out regional constraints (eu vs us vs apac) and KMS compatibility for private customers.
tamika: can we include a non-goal about not changing customer-visible model ids unless pinned? that's been a customer complaint.
mira: good point. draft bullets:
- Goal: ensure requests are routed to cheapest compatible model variant while meeting latency SLO and safety constraints.
- Customer asks captured: (1) deterministic route for pinned versions, (2) soft-fallback to quantized variants for cost savings, (3) strict data residency by region.
- Acceptance criteria (high level):
  * Routing decision respects customer pinning and tier affinity 100% of time in canary.
  * Fallbacks degrade gracefully: same API surface, <5% error increase on handled failovers.
  * No PII leaves region for private/vpc customers.
alex: nit: define "compatible" precisely. same family? same tokenizer? same output shape? we need a compatibility matrix.
mira: yep — will add formal matrix. quick pseudo example for compatibility check:
```
if model.arch == request.arch_family and model.max_seq >= req.seq and tokenizer.compat(request.tokenizer):
  candidate = true
else:
  candidate = false
```
jordan: also handle degenerate edge case where kv-cache incompat prevents resume — must fall back to cold-run with warning to app.
tamika: rollout strategy suggestion:
- Stage 1: internal canary (10% traffic, engineer opt-in) for 1 week
- Stage 2: gradual ramp to 25% across low-risk customers (no pinned versions)
- Stage 3: enterprise opt-ins and Dedicated fleets (manual enable)
sam: metrics to track: route-miss rate, fallback-rate, tail-latency P95/P99, cost-per-token delta, customer-impacting-errors.
mira: launch gates (must pass to GA):
1) Compatibility matrix complete and tested against 10 representative models.
2) Canary shows fallback-rate < 2% and <1% customer-visible errors for 7 days.
3) E2E test harness covers region routing and KMS flows.
4) Rollback path validated and automatable via console toggle.
alex: edge cases to call out in PRD:
- Model family changes after rollout (new tokenizer) -> require blacklist until model conversion.
- Region-wide capacity exhaustion -> multi-region failover policy with explicit customer opt-in.
- Partial response from model (stream cut) -> auto-retry to alternate variant up to N times.
mira: on customer asks: flagging two priority enterprise asks — strict pinned routing + audit log of fallback decisions. both map to config knobs in console.
jordan: for audit logs we need schema: timestamp, request_id, chosen_model, fallback_reason, latency, policy_version.
tamika: can we include a quick UI copy for console toggles? e.g., "Fallback behavior: Off / Conservative / Aggressive" with descriptions.
mira: yes — conservative = only identical architecture variants; aggressive = allow quantized/fast variants with potential quality delta.
sam: risk register quick:
- Wrong compatibility matching -> user-facing regressions (mitigation: model testbench)
- Cost regression if aggressive fallback chosen erroneously (mitigation: cost alarms + rollback)
- Security/regulatory breach if region routing misconfigured (mitigation: KMS integration tests + infra gating)
eng-bot: deploy-checklist created: https://redwood.tools/checks/PRD-4821 (auto)
mira: can people +1 the acceptance criteria and rollout plan? i'll land a PRD and RFC after thumbs-up.
alex: +1 from me. please add explicit test cases for tokenizer mismatch and kv-cache incompat.
jordan: +1, add audit log schema to infra tickets.
tamika: +1, and include a customer-facing opt-out timeline for noisy fallbacks.
sam: +1, add alert thresholds for cost delta and fallback-rate.
mira: thanks all — i'll update and open the RFC. tagging @eng-bot to create RFC draft ticket.
